jobs.description: Employer: Fairfax County Government Expires: 10/22/2026 This announcement may be used to fill multiple positions located within Region 1 area of Neighborhood and Community Services (NCS) at the following locations: Bush Hill Elementary School, 5927 Westchester St, Alexandria, VA 22310Cameron Elementary School, 3434 Campbell Dr, Alexandria, VA 22303Mount Eagle Elementary School, 6116 N Kings Hwy, Alexandria, VA 22303Join our team at the Department of Neighborhood and Community Services (NCS) and help support our mission to partner with communities, families, and individuals to provide opportunities to access a continuum of resources that promote equity and create positive outcomes for people of all ages and abilities. Our vision is to see connected communities where all individuals and families are supported and empowered to thrive.This position works as part of the Culture, Recreation, and Community Connections (CRCC) Division to deliver out-of-school-time care, recreation, and culturally enriching programs and daily hands-on activities for school-age youth with diverse functional, inclusive, cultural, and economic needs at assigned location(s), using human-centered and human development practices in a school-based setting. Exercises human-centered design principles to support participants’ experience and create access to opportunity through the creation of positive developmental relationships based on the individualized needs of school-age youth. Supports and promotes equity-based programs and practices that address needs and equitable access to opportunities that enhance well-being and community inclusion. Provides support to all children in the program, including children with special needs. The role requires a split-shift schedule Monday through Friday. On days when Fairfax County Public Schools (FCPS) is out of school (teacher workdays, winter break, spring break, summer), this position requires a full-day schedule of 6.5 or more consecutive hours. Fairfax County is home to a highly diverse population, with a significant number of residents speaking languages other than English at home (including Spanish, Asian/Pacific Islander, Indo-European, and many others.) We encourage candidates who are bilingual in English and another language to apply for this opportunity. Learn more about the work we do in NCS here. jobs.feedName: Michael D. Eisner College of Education
jobs.title: Mechanical Engineer (Robotics) at Tutor Intelligence
jobs.description: Employer: Tutor Intelligence Expires: 10/22/2026 About TutorWe believe general-purpose, generally-intelligent robots will be built in our lifetimes. Robots will work in our factories, move our goods, walk on our streets and eventually be in our homes. To build that future, research and deployment must work in lockstep: real-world operation must make the technology better and better technology must make deployment easier. We're looking for the thinkers, builders, and researchers who want to be part of that loop.As an AI robotics company that deploys its inventions directly into the facilities that need them, on state-of-the-art hardware, every line of code written at Tutor has a direct impact on the global, physical economy.Our CultureWe believe that something truly special can happen when talented, motivated people work together; at Tutor, every member of our team is empowered to have real impact in everything that they do. We’re characterized by both technical excellence and next-level collaboration and respect.What this role isWe are looking for someone who can own the entirety of a robot, or potential multiple different types of robots. In this role you will guide the work of other engineers, ensuring that development runs smoothly from napkin sketch through manufacturing and support.Some of this work will be you designing and prototyping. Some of it will be working with members of different teams and ensuring we build the right thing. Some of it will be mentoring and guiding other engineers, growing them into leaders and owners.This is a role for someone with strength in making things. You will be expected to know how every part of the robot works, and if you couldn't make it yourself, you certainly can figure out how one would and understand the tradeoffs involved.This is a job for someone who appreciates fast and methodical hardware iteration. You have likely spent time in places where things come to life in weeks/months before -clubs/teams, startups, labs, places where you can appreciate what a relatively small, talented team can do when motivated and excited to do so.About Our Roles & TitlesAt Tutor, we believe great engineers and researchers are defined by what they build and the impact they have — not where they sit in an org chart or what title they have. Therefore, everyone in our R&D org holds the title Member of Technical Staff (MoTS). Our job postings use standard titles so you can find us, but if you join Tutor, you'll be a MoTS — with a level that is determined through the interview process.That also means we hire people, not slots. Work at Tutor evolves every quarter, and we set the expectation of flexibility from day one — it's common for people to start on one thing and shift to another based on where the team needs them most. A high technical bar across the board is what makes that flexibility possible: it's what allows people to contribute meaningfully whatever problem they take on.

jobs.title: Montessori Toddler Support Teacher/Guide at Winfield Children's House
jobs.description: Employer: Winfield Children's House Expires: 10/22/2026 Winfield Children's House has an opening for a Support Toddler Teacher/Guide to join our team for the 2026-27 school year. This teacher will work in our Accredited Montessori program as part of our Toddler classrooms for children 16 months through 3 years. At Winfield we embrace the notion that every person brings value and importance, so we consider every role to be an integral part of our team. The position requires a thoughtful, nurturing, conscientious individual who has worked with young children and is passionate about Toddler education. The best support guides are self-starters, able to maintain a balance between essential daily tasks and flexibly responding to shifting needs throughout the day. You will come to anticipate and learn the rhythms of the classrooms and the children to know where you can provide the best help in any given moment. You will work with both of our Toddler classrooms, getting to know the all of the teachers and the children in both rooms, and becoming an integral part of our Toddler team.A Montessori credential or experience in a Montessori Toddler program is a plus, but not a requirement. More important is a recognition of the importance of a solid early childhood program, and a curiosity to learn more.Our Support Guides often move on to classroom teams in subsequent school years, or even pursue a Montessori credential, which Winfield sponsors teachers to attend. While taking that step is not a requirement, Winfield is committed to helping our teachers achieve their professional goals, so this position could be ideal if you are looking to further your career, or early in your journey, and exploring to find your ideal age group and setting.In addition to being a valued member of the Toddler team, and working with credentialed Montessorians in each classroom, you will part of the wider Winfield community made up of four Early Childhood classrooms for children 3-6 years old. Our full-time Outdoor Educator and Art teacher round out our talented and caring teaching staff.This position is full-time and year-round; during the summer months, a smaller nature and art camp is offered to our enrolled students, providing an opportunity for this position to join one of the camp teaching teams.The position is available now, but we can be flexible on the start date for the right candidate.Winfield is located in Falmouth, just north of Portland, Maine. Soon to be celebrating its 40th anniversary, Winfield currently serves approximately 100 students from 16 months through 6 years old. Read more about Montessori and our school online at www.winfieldhouse.net.Responsibilities:Follow schedules and routinesEstablish and maintain positive relationships with students, parents, and co-workersMaintain the health and safety of all studentsPrepare the classroom environment for optimal learningAttend meetings and staff developmentQualifications:A high school diploma or higher. Preferred is a Bachelor's or Associate degree, or some college work, ideally in an Early Childhood-related areaAt least one year of experience working with toddlers in childcare, teaching, or other related fieldsAbility to build rapport with childrenPositive and patient demeanorAbility to work on the floor or at a table with children, and to help children navigate up and down stairsExcellent written and verbal communication skillsThe ability to work collaboratively in a supportive environmentWinfield offers a competitive compensation and benefits package (including medical, dental, short-term disability, and life insurance), commensurate with experience. This position is eligible for participation in the Maine State Early Childhood Educator Workforce Salary Supplement program. The amount provided through that program is determined by the individual's education and experience, and is in addition to the salary range provided here.
